title: Material table
description: DESIGN.md §4.2. This file is the modding API described in §12.5 — 'a mod is a materials file' — so it is written as a public contract rather than an internal note. Every value is in game units, not SI: §3 lists physical accuracy as an explicit non-goal, and §4.2 asks only for monotonicity and consistent ratios.

tags.description: Role tags, in order. A material's index in this list is its bit, so appending is safe and reordering is not. Reactions match on these rather than on material identity, which is what keeps the interaction matrix authorable without an N² table (§4.2).

classes.description: Taxonomy only. §4.2: 'no mechanical effect'. Used for the base hue in §10.1 and for nothing else.

hardness.description: Stress a part sustains before it deforms. Zero means fluid: no deformation threshold and no fracture, only displacement.

toughness.description: Resistance to fracture. §4.2: hardness up / toughness down is the normal relationship, and a material that breaks it is automatically interesting and should be rare.

elasticity.description: Fraction of arriving mechanical energy handed straight back rather than absorbed.

friction.description: Fraction of absorbed mechanical energy that becomes heat. This is why grinding warms things.

conductivity.description: Charge transfer. Also decides which nearby part an over-threshold arc reaches for.

aether_permeability.description: How readily fields pass through. High permeability makes a good conduit and a poor battery.

discharge_threshold.description: Charge held before arcing. Should not exceed aether_capacity.

phaseTemps.description: Threshold temperatures. `melt`, `boil` and `ignite` are crossed on the way up; `solidify` is crossed on the way down and is this implementation's one addition to the §4.2 schema (without it nothing can freeze). Omit or null a transition a material does not have.

phaseProducts.description: What the part becomes. Every transition with a temperature needs one.

phaseEnergy.description: Latent energy per unit volume. For melt/boil/solidify this is the size of the plateau the part holds at while the transition is paid for, and a reversible pair must not net positive around the loop — tools/fuzz.ts decides that. For ignite it is the chemical energy released, and it is what makes a fire hotter than the thing that lit it.

with.description: Tag pattern the arriving reagent must carry, written `*:tagname`.

rate.description: Volume converted per unit of corrosive potential, before the target's corrosion resistance.

thermal.description: Energy per unit volume converted. Negative absorbs — an endothermic reaction is a cold weapon.

formation.description: §5.1 layer 6: which conditions can produce this material. Carried through validation and deliberately not packed into the simulation — worldgen is M2, and §12.5 says not to foreclose it.
